Testimony of the Maine Public Utilities Commission
In Support of
LD 906, An Act to Update the Solar Energy Development Reporting Date Deadline
March 26, 2025
Senator Lawrence, Representative Sachs, and Distinguished Members of the Joint Standing Committee
on Energy, Utilities, and Technology (Committee), my name is Deirdre Schneider, testifying in support of LD 906, An Act to Update the Solar Energy Development Reporting Date Deadline on behalf of the
Public Utilities Commission (Commission).
LD 906 moves the date for a report required pursuant to 35-A M.R.S. � 3473, subsection l-A from
January ls` to February 10"` . The report is required to look at the costs and benefits from solar energy development and must include at a minimum:
I Revenue from the sale of renewable energy credits; I Societal benefits through avoided greenhouse gas emissions; I Reduced electricity prices; and I Avoided or reduced costs associated with:
o Electricity capacity requirements; o Environmental compliance requirements;
Portfolio requirements established in section 3210;
Renewable energy credit price suppression; and Electricity transmission and distribution costs.
Since the report is looking at information from the previous calendar year, the January ls` reporting date requires some assumptions because there is not sufficient time to analyze the data through
December 31$` . Moving the reporting date to February 10"` allows the necessary time to more fully analyze information and avoids the inclusion of some assumptions in the final report.
l would be happy to answer any questions or provide additional information for the work session.

Testimony of Senator Mark W. Lawrence introducing
LD 906, An Act to Update the Solar Energy Development Reporting Date Deadline
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Energy, Utilities and Technology March 26, 2025
Chair Sachs and esteemed colleagues of the Joint Standing Committee on Energy, Utilities and
Technology, my name is Mark Lawrence. I am the State Senator from District 35, proudly representing Eliot, Kittery, Ogunquit, South Berwick, and York. I am here to present LD 906, An
Act to Update the Solar Energy Development Reporting Date Deadline.
This bill proposes to change the date from January 1 of each year to February 10 of each year for the submission of the report from the Public Utilities Commission regarding the monitoring of the level of solar energy development in the State.
As you'll hear from the representatives of the Public Utilities Commission, the analysis required from the previous year requires more time than current statute calls for.
The report encapsulates quite a bit of date including but not limited to: Revenue from the sale of renewable energy credits; Societal benefits through avoided greenhouse gas emissions; Reduced electricity prices; and Avoided or reduced costs associated with:
a. Electricity capacity requirements; b. Environmental compliance requirements;
. Portfolio requirements established in section 3210;
Renewable energy credit price suppression; and . Electricity transmission and distribution costs.
With the year ending on December 31 and the report being due on January 1, due to the way the
current statute is written, the PUC may have to make their most informed projections on the
Solar Energy Report. As you can see above, the report is robust and captures quite a bit of data to help inform the Legislature as we create policy.
Thank you for the opportunity to present this bill. I am happy to answer questions you may have
for me and would defer questions about specifics to the representatives from the PUC that are
here today.
